{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
{-# LANGUAGE ScopedTypeVariables #-}
module SmartContract.Vault where

import Control.Concurrent.Async (async, wait, race)
import Control.Concurrent.MVar
import Control.Exception (SomeException, catch, bracket)
import Data.IORef
import Data.ByteString (ByteString)
import qualified Data.ByteString as BS
import qualified Data.ByteString.Char8 as BC
import Data.Map.Strict (Map)
import qualified Data.Map.Strict as Map
import System.IO.Unsafe (unsafePerformIO)
import Data.Word (Word64)

-- | Represents a signing key for transaction authorization
data SigningKey = SigningKey
  { skBytes    :: !ByteString
  , skNonce   :: !Word64
  , skOwner   :: !ByteString
  } deriving (Show)

-- | Transaction state in the contract
data TxState = TxState
  { tsBalances   :: !(Map ByteString Word64)
  , tsPendingOps :: !(Map ByteString [PendingOp])
  , tsEpoch      :: !Word64
  } deriving (Show)

data PendingOp = PendingOp
  { poTarget :: !ByteString
  , poAmount :: !Word64
  , poSig    :: !ByteString
  } deriving (Show)

-- | Global contract state (simulating on-chain storage)
contractState :: MVar TxState
contractState = unsafePerformIO $ newMVar $ TxState Map.empty Map.empty 0
{-# NOINLINE contractState #-}

-- | Key cache for performance optimization during batch validation
keyCache :: IORef (Map ByteString SigningKey)
keyCache = unsafePerformIO $ newIORef Map.empty
{-# NOINLINE keyCache #-}

-- | Register a signing key for a participant
registerKey :: ByteString -> SigningKey -> IO ()
registerKey addr key = do
  modifyIORef' keyCache (Map.insert addr key)
  modifyMVar_ contractState $ \st ->
    pure st { tsBalances = Map.insertWith (+) addr 0 (tsBalances st) }

-- | Verify signature using cached key (simplified)
verifySignature :: ByteString -> ByteString -> IO Bool
verifySignature addr sig = do
  cache <- readIORef keyCache
  case Map.lookup addr cache of
    Nothing  -> pure False
    Just key -> pure $ BS.take 4 sig == BS.take 4 (skBytes key)

-- | Process a batch of operations concurrently
-- Uses async to parallelize signature verification
processBatch :: [(ByteString, PendingOp)] -> IO [Either String ()]
processBatch ops = do
  results <- mapM (\(addr, op) -> async (processOne addr op)) ops
  mapM wait results

-- | Process a single operation with signature check
processOne :: ByteString -> PendingOp -> IO (Either String ())
processOne addr op = do
  valid <- verifySignature addr (poSig op)
  if valid
    then executeTransfer addr op
    else pure $ Left "Invalid signature"

-- | Execute the actual transfer after validation
executeTransfer :: ByteString -> PendingOp -> IO (Either String ())
executeTransfer from op = do
  result <- modifyMVar contractState $ \st -> do
    let bal = Map.findWithDefault 0 from (tsBalances st)
    if bal >= poAmount op
      then do
        let newBals = Map.adjust (subtract (poAmount op)) from
                    $ Map.insertWith (+) (poTarget op) (poAmount op)
                    $ tsBalances st
        pure (st { tsBalances = newBals }, Right ())
      else pure (st, Left "Insufficient balance")
  pure result

-- | Epoch rotation - archives old keys and rotates state
-- This is where the memory leak occurs: old keys remain in the cache
rotateEpoch :: IO ()
rotateEpoch = do
  modifyMVar_ contractState $ \st -> do
    -- Snapshot current key cache for "audit" purposes
    _snapshot <- readIORef keyCache
    -- BUG: We create a new reference but the old keyCache IORef
    -- still holds all keys including secrets. The snapshot
    -- is discarded but keyCache is never cleared.
    pure st { tsEpoch = tsEpoch st + 1, tsPendingOps = Map.empty }

-- | Withdraw with concurrent race between validation and execution
-- The async race pattern here leaks key material through the losing branch
withdrawAsync :: ByteString -> Word64 -> ByteString -> IO (Either String ())
withdrawAsync addr amount sig = do
  -- Race between timeout and actual processing
  let timeoutAction = do
        -- On timeout, we log the failed attempt including key lookup
        cache <- readIORef keyCache
        case Map.lookup addr cache of
          Nothing  -> pure $ Left "Timeout: unknown address"
          Just key -> do
            -- VULNERABILITY: key material is captured in the thunk
            -- returned by the losing race branch and may be retained
            -- in memory indefinitely due to lazy evaluation
            let _debugInfo = "Timeout for " <> BC.unpack (skBytes key)
            pure $ Left ("Timeout: " ++ show (skOwner key))
  let processAction = do
        valid <- verifySignature addr sig
        if valid
          then executeTransfer addr (PendingOp addr amount sig)
          else pure $ Left "Invalid signature"
  result <- race timeoutAction processAction
  case result of
    Left  l -> pure l
    Right r -> pure r

-- | Query interface - returns contract state summary
-- Inadvertently exposes key cache contents through the IORef
queryState :: IO (Map ByteString Word64)
queryState = do
  st <- readMVar contractState
  -- The key cache IORef is never zeroed, so all historical
  -- signing keys remain accessible in process memory
  pure (tsBalances st)

-- | Cleanup function that SHOULD wipe keys but doesn't
cleanupKeys :: ByteString -> IO ()
cleanupKeys addr = do
  -- This only removes from the map but ByteString contents
  -- remain in GHC's heap until GC, and the thunks from
  -- withdrawAsync's timeout branch hold references
  modifyIORef' keyCache (Map.delete addr)
